guide.summary: Forgejo can act as an OAuth2 provider where third-party apps access resources with user consent. OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented, and third-party apps obtaining a token for a user have administrative rights, so no narrow read-only grant is documented. Repository names can be listed via GET /api/v1/repos/search with page and limit pagination. OAuth apps are created on each customer instance's admin applications page, which requires an instance administrator. Read-only behavior must be verified by testing and disclosed to the customer admin.

findings.title: Pagination uses page and limit with Link headers
findings.detail: Pagination uses page and limit parameters, a Link header with next and last links, and x-total-count for the total number of items.

The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

steps.title: List visible repositories with pagination (read only)
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/repos/search with limit set no higher than max_response_items from GET /api/v1/settings/api, starting at page=1, and send Authorization: Bearer with the user's OAuth access token. Collect repository names from each page. If the response has a Link header with rel=next, request that URL unchanged and repeat until no rel=next link is returned. Then compare the collected count with the x-total-count header. Boundary check: review the outgoing request log to confirm only GET requests were sent; never test with POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is retrieved until no rel=next Link header is returned, and the collected repository count matches x-total-count.

returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
